issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters (returns int), but the solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This parameterized signature deviates from the specified API and will confuse students (and break tests) because they are expected to implement/call a no-argument method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution conform to the specification by providing a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total (decide whether guests are included by default per spec). Alternatively, if the boolean parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) and adjust the template/tests accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the method signature and expected usage: students and tests expecting a no-arg method (as described in the exercise) will not find the matching implementation in the solution, creating a mapping and usage confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by providing a no-argument getTotalNumberOfStudents() method that returns the intended total (e.g. including guest students if that is the specified behavior). If the boolean variant is useful, add it as an overloaded helper (getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)) but keep the parameterless signature declared in the UML so students and tests can map to it.
